entities.summary: Jerónimo Merino Cob, alias El Cura Merino, was a Spanish guerrilla fighter and priest who played a significant role in the Peninsular War (1808-1814) and the fight for Spanish independence from Napoleon's France. Born in Villoviado, Aragon, Spain in 1769, Merino Cob joined the Spanish resistance against Napoleon's occupation and participated in several key battles, including the Battle of Zaragoza. He also served as a priest and helped to organize the resistance movement in the region. Merino Cob's actions contributed to the eventual defeat of Napoleon's forces and the restoration of Spanish independence. He died in 1844 at the age of 75. Merino Cob's legacy as a hero of the Spanish resistance has endured, and he remains a celebrated figure in Spanish history and culture.
